page_title: Build Forms, APIs, and Agentic Workflows with One Self-Hosted Developer Productivity Platform - Form.io

sources.entry: form.io - A REST API building platform that utilizes a drag & drop form builder, and is application framework agnostic. Contains open source and enterprise version. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.name: Form.io
summary.one_liner: Form.io is a self-hostable developer platform for building drag-and-drop forms, submission APIs, and governed data workflows, with an open source version and enterprise editions.
use_cases: Building intake and onboarding forms for internal applications
Generating REST APIs from form definitions
Converting fillable or scanned PDFs into web forms
Adding audited digital signatures to submitted records
Offering self-service form building to customers in a multi-tenant product
Creating interactive reports from submission data in an app
summary.what_it_does: Form.io lets developers define a form once as a JSON schema, which then generates a submission API, validation, and permissions for that data. Forms can be embedded in applications via JavaScript and styled with custom CSS, and support conditional logic, multi-step wizards, external data sources, and post-submit form actions such as email, webhooks, and integrations. It offers PDF rendering and templates from submissions, a visual reporting layer built on MongoDB aggregation, and signing that binds signatures to field values and form revision. The page also describes an MCP server and Claude Code plugin so AI coding agents can build against a self-hosted deployment.
notable: Form schema defines the form, API, validation, and permissions together
Revision history with field-level change tracking and per-version rendering of submissions
Self-hosted; AI agent access stays inside the customer's security boundary
Open source and enterprise versions, listed on awesome-selfhosted under MIT license
caveats: Enterprise features such as security compliance, PDF servers, and the embedded builder module are sold as paid tiers with pricing on a separate page
Listing describes an open source edition under MIT, but the page itself centers on paid enterprise plans
